## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kumārapetavatthu* (Pv 30) is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The work addresses how one escapes an evil past [SuttaCentral], illustrating the torments experienced by beings in consequence of sinful deeds committed in previous lives [Law 1926], including the motif of adultery resulting in an unfortunate ghostly rebirth [Clark 1994]. A verse cited by Seishi Karashima (Pv 453) recounts the miraculous preservation of an infant abandoned in a charnel ground who is protected from dangerous beings and sustained by virtue of past merit (*katapuññakumāra*) [Karashima 2012].
SuttaCentral lists four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Automated text analysis by DharmaNexus records extensive Pali-internal text reuse between the *Kumārapetavatthu* and the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, consisting of 19 matching passages (3,157 shared characters, including a long passage matching verses 7.4–11.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects machine-level cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Śrīsena-avadāna* (D0349), though these represent low-confidence automatic matches rather than curated parallels [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0507a) (§7.4–11.4 ↔ §2033–2043)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): དཔལ་གྱི་སྡེའི་རྟོགས་པ་བརྗོད་པ། (śrīsena-avadāna) (D0349) [bo]
